title: A trick that made AI-assisted motion & animation tuning way better for me: automated PlayMode sequence strips
author: Brave-History-6502
selftext:
Dynamic player driven animation is super tricky still to get working with agents.

My fix has been making tests dump **multi-frame sequence strips** (like this 11-frame snowboard nose-press butter) plus looping GIF/MP4 clips after every run. Both my assistant and I can immediately spot exact frames where a pose pops, weight hangs behind the board, or camera follow lags, then tighten curves and timing on the next pass.

**Live interactive sequence example (0.25x/0.5x/1x speed, `-1f`/`+1f` step, contact strip + GIF/MP4):**
https://play.gamecrew.ai/seq/e_6yMQmOU49Vdgk5WpUPBrcMliU6qQiQ/

I also exposed my open asset & technique tools over MCP with two connection options:
- **Free, zero login (Open Library & Techniques):** `https://play.gamecrew.ai/mcp/library`
  838 CC0/CC BY 3D models, seamless PBR textures & audio, 58 verified Unity 6 / Godot 4 / Three.js guides, and offline engine API lookup — no account or token needed:
  ```bash
  claude mcp add --transport http gamecrew-library https://play.gamecrew.ai/mcp/library
  ```
- **Optional free sign-in (Add techniques or beta test my cloud build & sequence loop):** `https://play.gamecrew.ai/mcp`
  Google OAuth login if you have technique guides to contribute or want to beta test my cloud compiles, PlayMode sequence strips, and Blender/Unity animation checks (full setup: https://play.gamecrew.ai/developers#connect).

Try out the game here too if you are interested in the game in the example: https://play.gamecrew.ai/play/bottomless

comments.author: ScrywareDev
comments.body: This is close to what I ended up doing for sprite work. Single frames kept lying to me. A pose looks fine frozen and then the cycle reads wrong the second it moves. I have the test runs dump the full strip now and I judge that instead. How are you triggering yours, on every change or only when a test run finishes? And do the strips catch timing problems for you, or mostly pose problems?

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body: Both since they catch the temp of the movement as well. But I've mostly used it to catch pose probelms. Right now I use it primarily when working on things involving dynamic movement and isn't baked to heavily into test runs... though you could use the output almost like a "snapshot" test.

replies.author: ScrywareDev
replies.body: Dynamic movement is exactly where mine lie the worst. A walk cycle can look right frame by frame and still feel off at speed. When a strip shows you a timing problem, do you retime what you have or go back and redo poses? I end up redoing more than I expected.
